item.title: Delimitation, NEET & Cauvery: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay discussed with Amit Shah
item.description: Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah, Vijay, who is also the council's vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states which have successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation. He said the issue had become particularly important as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census nears its end.

item.title: 8-0 becomes 8-1: 'Impatient' PV Sindhu falls to cramping Wang Zhi Yi in epic duel
item.description: PV Sindhu's World Championships campaign ended in controversy as Wang Zhi Yi overcame cramps, a hostile Delhi crowd and the five-time medallist to snap her unbeaten record against Chinese shuttlers at the Worlds. Ayush Shetty also bowed out, while Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand and Satwik-Chirag marched into the quarter-finals.

item.title: Gates Foundation makes landmark 10-yr donation to Washington University to strengthen ...
item.description: The Gates Foundation has awarded a significant donation to the University of Washington's health institute. This substantial grant will expand the Global Burden of Disease study's reach. IHME will now cover nearly 5,000 locations, providing more detailed local health information. The funding also supports health forecasting and global health spending research efforts. This investment aims to inform critical decisions for improving global health outcomes.

item.title: How an ex-Buddhist monk & Meta engineer founded a startup that now rivals Accenture
item.description: Lilly Chen, a former Buddhist monk and Meta software engineer, founded Contenda after a hackathon. She and three friends turned a pandemic-era project into a successful startup. The company focuses on helping businesses repurpose technical content effectively. Contenda secured one million dollars in pre-seed funding in March 2021. Chen now leads the company as its chief executive officer.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: ABVP, Left-leaning student groups clash on Jadavpur University campus; several injured
item.description: A clash erupted between ABVP and Left student groups at Jadavpur University early Thursday. Several students sustained injuries during the confrontation, with some requiring hospital treatment. The confrontation reportedly began over a student union meeting and continued late into the night. Both groups accused each other of bringing outsiders onto the university campus. Protests have been announced by both student organizations following the incident.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: In the 1970s, man bought part of Washington island; now he's its only resident
item.description: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Engineer built Ozarks hillside home in 1970; son restores it 50 years later
item.description: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Canadian wildfires cut solar power by 6.38 TWh, caused $1.9bn loss in 2023
item.description: Wildfire smoke significantly reduced solar power generation across North America and Europe. This reduction caused substantial economic losses and increased carbon emissions. Other air pollution sources like automobiles also impact solar panel productivity. Wildfires can also physically damage solar farm equipment and infrastructure. Improved forecasting and vegetation management can mitigate these solar generation challenges.

item.title: Why UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi' matters more than ever in 2027 assembly election
item.description: Uttar Pradesh elections now prioritize women voters, who are a significant electoral force. Women's turnout has consistently surpassed men's in recent polls. Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers. Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters. Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.
item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE

item.title: H-1B visa reality for Indians: Unpredictable costs, tougher odds & greater risks
item.description: H-1B visas have long been the main road for Indian professionals who are seeking employment, long-term career opportunities, and eventually even the green card in the US. But over the past two years, several changes in the H-1B visa application and selection criterion have added a huge layer of uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Dan Ticktum targets GEN4 seat and Formula E Championship success
item.description: Cupra Kiro driver Dan Ticktum has expressed his desire to race in Formula E’s GEN4 era, which begins with Season 13 in December. However, the British driver is yet to secure a seat with Cupra Kiro or any other team for the upcoming season. In a video shared after the London E-Prix, Ticktum reflected on the season gone by, discussed his difficult weekend in London and shared his hopes for the future.

item.title: Man posing as transgender sexually assaults air hostess on pretext of 'curing evil eye'
item.description: A 25-year-old air hostess was sexually assaulted after a man gained entry to her flat. The accused impersonated a transgender person and claimed to perform a ritual for warding off evil. Police arrested Anil Shinde, 28, within four hours after tracing his movements via CCTV. Shinde also collected Rs 200 from the victim before fleeing the scene. Authorities are investigating if Shinde has committed similar offenses previously.
item.dc:creator: NARAYAN NAMBOODIRI

item.title: After Rana’s demise, Oly medallist Manu forging new bonds with Serbian coach
item.description: Paris Olympics double medallist Manu Bhaker is showing a more flexible approach as she prepares for the 2028 Los Angeles Games. After coach Jaspal Rana’s sudden death, Bhaker has adapted to Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic’s methods, spending over eight hours training daily. Jelena says Bhaker’s openness to new ideas reflects her hunger to improve, with the 24-year-old focused on becoming better and more consistent.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: ‘Maybe that was her tactic’: Sindhu questions ‘cramps’; Wang says ‘I was injured’
item.description: PV Sindhu lost her World Championships pre-quarterfinal match to Wang Zhi Yi. The Indian player questioned if her opponent's late cramps were tactical. Wang Zhi Yi insisted her cramps were genuine and rejected any tactical suggestions. Sindhu felt she should have been more patient during crucial points. The defeat ended Sindhu's unbeaten record against Chinese players at the event.

item.title: Joe Root equals Sachin Tendulkar’s record for most fifties in Test cricket
item.description: Joe Root achieved a significant milestone by equaling Sachin Tendulkar's record for most Test half-centuries. He scored his 68th fifty during England's first Test against Pakistan at Headingley. Root and Cox built a crucial partnership to give England a first-innings lead. England's pace bowlers, Robinson and Tongue, took five wickets each to dismiss Pakistan. The team secured a first-innings lead after bowling Pakistan out for 171.

item.title: 2.98 lakh URLs sent for takedown; I4C flags scams, CSAM and other unlawful content
item.description: Government departments requested removal of nearly 2.98 lakh URLs from social media platforms. States accounted for the majority of these takedown requests, sending 2.44 lakh URLs. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre flagged over 51,000 URLs related to various scams. This action follows widespread student protests and content blocking reports on social media. Government rules were amended to expedite the removal of unlawful online content.
item.dc:creator: TOI NEWS DESK

item.title: Hockey World Cup: India hold England to goalless draw, seal second-round spot
item.description: India advanced to the second round of the Women's Hockey World Cup after a tense draw. They held England to a 0-0 score, securing second place in their group. China topped Pool D with seven points, while England was eliminated from the competition. India's goalkeeper Bichu Devi made a crucial save in the final seconds. The team progressed with an unbeaten record of two draws and one win.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.description: Economic think tank Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said the change means eligible rupee payments for exports to countries other than Nepal and Bhutan will now qualify for FTP benefits and can also be counted towards meeting export obligations.

item.title: Premier League 2026/27: Everything you need to know ahead of the new season
item.description: The 2026/27 Premier League season begins with Arsenal defending their title and three promoted clubs returning to the top flight. With nine English clubs competing in Europe, another fiercely contested title race and battles for European qualification and survival expected, the new campaign promises plenty of drama. Here’s everything you need to know, including key statistics, players, managers and opening fixtures.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 6-year-old student slapped over homework, dies after collapsing in teacher's lap
item.description: A six-year-old boy collapsed and died in a classroom at a private school. His family alleges a teacher beat him for not completing his homework assignment. The incident, captured on video, shows the teacher admonishing and slapping the student. The boy was declared dead after being brought to KG Hospital. Police and officials are investigating the circumstances surrounding the tragic death.
item.dc:creator: NALLA RAM BABU

item.title: India's solar story: Cell shortage may be short-lived as capacity set to tripple
item.description: India is set to boost its solar cell production capability in the near future. This project is designed to comply with local-content regulations and to close the existing supply deficiencies. By December 2027, a noticeable increase in cell output is anticipated, driven by new investments aimed at ensuring long-term energy resilience. The market is evolving to meet local demands, effectively alleviating supply issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: 'Hi' trailer: Nayanthara & Kavin’s love story gets a twist ahead of Aug 28 release
item.description: The much-anticipated trailer for 'Hi,' a romance drama starring Nayanthara and Kavin, has just been released. Directed by Vishnu Edavan, this film, hitting theaters on August 28, follows Kavin's quest for love as he encounters Nayanthara, a woman challenging societal norms. Their unlikely marriage journey unfolds, offering a heartfelt exploration of love and companionship, joined by a talented cast including Bhagyaraj, Prabhu, and Radikaa Sarathkumar.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: US Open sets tennis history with record $5.5m prize for singles champions
item.description: The 2026 US Open will offer a record $108 million in player compensation. Singles champions will each receive $5.5 million, a significant increase from previous years. Even first-round losers will earn a record $140,000, reflecting broader prize money hikes. A new player support program and a Grand Slam Player Council were also announced. This initiative aims to strengthen financial support and player involvement in tournament decisions.

item.title: ICC makes U-turn on Gaddafi Stadium pitch demerit point
item.description: The ICC has withdrawn the demerit point given to Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium pitch after reviewing an appeal by the PCB. The Appeals Panel examined match footage, referee reports and captains’ comments before finding the pitch satisfactory. It said the surface did not show excessive unevenness, seam movement or spin. Pakistan had won the ODI series 2-1.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Jaayjeet Banerjee escapes serious injury after lorry hits car
item.description: Bengali actor Jaayjeet Banerjee was involved in a troubling accident near Tollygunge Karunamoyee Bridge when a speeding lorry collided with his car while he descended towards Haridevpur. Although the damage was substantial on the right side of his vehicle, Banerjee escaped without severe injuries. He has filed a report with the police and is anxious about the lorry driver’s well-being, urging Kolkata Police to take necessary actions.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Amit Shah hails South's development in CMs meet, cites 3 pillars of progress
item.description: Chairing the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Tamil Nadu's Mahabalipuram, the Union home minister said: "The people of South India and the governments have also established many excellent traditions in the fields of innovation and revenue generation." He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: East Bengal break 40-year-old record, register India’s biggest-ever win in Asia
item.description: In a stunning display of skill, East Bengal FC triumphed over Rovers FC with a remarkable 12-0 scoreline during the AFC Women's Champions League. This victory is notable as it sets a record for the highest win by an Indian club in any Asian competition. The Moshal Girls now eagerly anticipate their next match against Sabah FA, needing just one more win to secure their place in the group stage.

item.title: Ohanna says she was pushed out: Actor alleges she was indirectly made to quit
item.description: Ohanna Shivanand, known earlier as Shilpa Anand, candidly addressed her sudden exit from the beloved series Dill Mill Gayye. She revealed that her departure was not by choice but stemmed from an unfortunate incident that occurred during a makeup room shift, leading to feelings of compromised self-respect. Despite the circumstances, she expressed that she has no resentment towards the show's producer.
